title: Artemis Financials — private deployment intake and region gating
summary: Initial discovery focused on private/VPC deployment requirements for a regulated financial workflow. Main concerns: region-based data residency, egress IP control, KMS integration, private endpoints vs peering, and end-to-end latency for inference. Agreed to share network checklist, IP ranges, security pack; customer to supply network team contact and region list. Schedule pilot benchmark for Q1.
topics: egress IPs / NAT and firewall rules
region residency and model hosting locations
KMS/HSM key integration and audit logs
performance and latency SLOs for inference
next_steps: Jordan to send private deployment network checklist and IP CIDR template (by 2028-01-17)
Priya to propose benchmark plan and sample workloads (by 2028-01-19)
Artemis to provide allowed region list and primary VPC contact (by 2028-01-18)
Share SOC2 and encryption whitepaper link (Jordan)

Priya Nair: Draft pilot benchmark plan + expected token volumes (due 2028-01-19)
Ravi Patel: Provide VPC peering contact, CIDR plan, and region restrictions (due 2028-01-18)

header: Date: 2028-01-15 | Start: 17:30 UTC | Duration: 58m | Meeting title: Artemis Financials - private deployment intake and region gating | Recording: yes
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Kim: hey everyone, thanks for joining. can you all hear me?
[00:05] Ravi Patel: yes, good morning for us, afternoon for you, thanks.
[00:08] Jordan Kim: cool. quick intro — i'm Jordan from Redwood, ae for this account, Priya is our se and Liam is joining on the solutions side. could each of you do a quick intro?
[00:18] Marta Alvarez: Marta, security architect, i'm mainly focused on encryption, key mgmt and audit logging for anything external.
[00:22] Yusuf Khan: Yusuf, s r e, i'll be the person configuring vpcs and peering.
[00:25] Claire DuPont: Claire, product, i'll be helping define success criteria for latency and throughput.
[00:30] Jordan Kim: great. goal for today — understand your network constraints, compliance gates, and what would allow a pilot vs prod deployment for private inference.
[00:40] Ravi Patel: to give background, we're a payments analytics firm, lots of pii and transaction data, regulators want data never to leave the eu for eu customers and same for apac. we also have strict egress controls for any third party.
[00:55] Priya Nair: ok, so region residency is a big one; do you have existing cloud regions and preferred model hosting locations?
[01:01] Ravi Patel: we have primary vpcs in eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1, some backups in us-east-1 but customer data for eu must stay in eu. ideally models serving eu traffic live in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1.
[01:14] Jordan Kim: Redwood supports model placement by region and you can pin a model version per region; for private deployments we can host entire control plane inside your vpc or run a private control plane with private endpoints. Marta, on KMS — do you manage keys in AWS KMS/HSM?
[01:30] Marta Alvarez: yes, we use a third-party HSM through CloudKMS and we need a Bring-Your-Own-Key flow with customer-managed keys and key rotation audit logs. encryption at rest and in transit both mandatory.
[01:40] Priya Nair: we have an integration path for CMEK with AWS KMS and for external HSMs too; audit logs can be forwarded to your SIEM. i'll capture the exact artifacts to send.
[01:48] Yusuf Khan: on the networking side, our main questions — do you need vpc peering or can you do private endpoint style? also what ip ranges, will there be static egress ips?
[01:57] Priya Nair: good question. we support a couple of private connectivity modes: 1) VPC peering / transit gateway (customer-managed peering) where Redwood nodes sit in your private subnets, 2) Private endpoints (privatelink-style) where endpoints are published and you use endpoint interfaces, or 3) dedicated on-prem gateway for air-gapped installs. each has tradeoffs.
[02:18] Claire DuPont: what are the latency differences? we have a 150ms p95 requirement for real-time scoring — is that achievable in eu region?
[02:27] Priya Nair: yes, if the model is hosted in-region and you run a minimal batch size, p95 of 100-150ms for small models is typical; for larger LLMs it's higher — depends on model variant and GPU type. we can run benchmarks.
[02:40] Ravi Patel: our traffic is bursty — spikes during settlement windows. we need predictable throughput during those windows. does dedicated capacity give better predictability?
[02:49] Jordan Kim: Dedicated pools absolutely — you get reserved GPU capacity and throughput SLAs. Dedicated inside your VPC (private deployment with reserved instances) gives the most predictable latency and throughput.
[03:00] Marta Alvarez: circling back to egress — we can't accept dynamic source IPs. we need a set of fixed egress IPs for firewall allowlisting, or we'll use an interface endpoint that doesn't egress publicly.
[03:10] Priya Nair: we can publish static egress IP ranges for instances inside the deployment or you can use private endpoints with no public egress. we'll provide the CIDR blocks and NAT gateway options; for transit gateway peering there's also options to NAT at your edge.
[03:22] Yusuf Khan: do you need route table changes or will the endpoints be reachable via AWS PrivateLink? some security teams allow only PrivateLink.
[03:28] Priya Nair: we support both. PrivateLink avoids route-table changes and keeps everything interface endpoint based; peering/transit is typically simpler for high-throughput low-latency traffic but requires route propagation and potential IP planning.
[03:40] Ravi Patel: any differences in monitorability and tracing? we need token-level cost and latency breakdowns and tracing hooks integrated with our observability stack.
[03:49] Liam O'Connor: from the solutions side, we push metrics and traces to customer endpoints via OTLP or can integrate with your Datadog/Prometheus endpoints. logs can be forwarded to S3 inside your account if you'd like.
[03:59] Marta Alvarez: audit log retention is legal requirement — 7 years on some events. can you guarantee persistence?
[04:05] Jordan Kim: we typically forward audit logs to customer-managed S3 or your SIEM, retention is controlled by you. we'll include the log-forwarding guide in the security pack.
[04:13] Claire DuPont: what about model artifacts and replication across regions — if we pin models in eu-west but you have a backup in us-east, how do you ensure no eu data crosses over?
[04:22] Priya Nair: we offer model variants and region pinning. replication for models is for performance only and can be disabled. data egress policies can be enforced so that requests containing eu data are routed only to eu-hosted instances.
[04:36] Ravi Patel: good. one more: compliance scanning and pen tests — we need to know what scope Redwood allows for pentest and if you'll sign an NDA.
[04:44] Jordan Kim: we can share our security engagement process; we sign NDAs and have a pen-test coordinate flow. i'll include the security engagement doc.
[04:50] Yusuf Khan: bandwidth cost during spikes — will we get unexpected charges? we need to understand egress billing.
[04:57] Priya Nair: if you host inside your VPC with private instances, data transfer stays in your account and is subject to your cloud billing. If you hit Redwood-hosted egress (managed hosted), data egress costs can apply; we'll include a cost model. Dedicated in your VPC avoids vendor egress charges but you'll pay for reserved capacity.
[05:12] Claire DuPont: okay, what does a pilot look like — timeline and success metrics?
[05:17] Priya Nair: typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: Week 0 - network setup and IP allowlisting, Week 1 - deploy model and run synthetic workload, Week 2 - run production shadow traffic and compare latency/cost, Week 3 - finalize runbook and handoff. success metrics: p95 latency under 150ms, throughput at peak window, no data egress outside allowed regions, integration with KMS.
[05:37] Ravi Patel: for the network changes, our security team needs an explicit checklist we can hand to infra.
[05:42] Jordan Kim: we'll send a one-page checklist with required CIDRs, ports, private endpoint instructions, and sample route tables.
[05:49] Marta Alvarez: also include the KMS key policy example and what logs we'll receive.
[05:53] Priya Nair: noted. we'll include key policy templates and the audit event fields you'll get.
[05:58] Yusuf Khan: do you provide github-style terraform modules for quick provisioning?
[06:03] Liam O'Connor: yes, we maintain terraform modules and cloudformation snippets for private deployments and endpoint creation. we'll surface the repo link.
[06:12] Claire DuPont: i'd like to hear more about fallback modes — if a regional pool is saturated, do requests fail or route to a different region? that's a regulatory problem for us.
[06:21] Priya Nair: by default we keep region routing strict, but you can opt-in for cross-region fallback; for Artemis we recommend strict routing for eu traffic, and add a canary fallback to a eu backup if you approve. fallback would be restricted to pinned eu replica only — not us.
[06:40] Ravi Patel: is there a service account model and fine-grained RBAC we can integrate with our idp?
[06:46] Jordan Kim: yes, we integrate with SAML SSO and support role-based access. for private deployments you can map roles to your internal teams; audit trails include token-level activity.
[06:56] Marta Alvarez: what about monthly usage reports for finance?
[06:59] Jordan Kim: Redwood Console provides per-token cost breakdown and exports; we'll include sample exports.
[07:06] Yusuf Khan: any gotchas with NAT gateway scaling? if we have 10k connections during spike will that break anything?
[07:12] Priya Nair: connection scaling is usually at the NAT/proxy layer; we provide guidance to size NAT or use multiple private subnets; Dedicated helps avoid excessive NAT churn as traffic stays local to deployed instances.
[07:25] Claire DuPont: ok this has been super helpful. final wrap — can we summarize actions?
[07:30] Jordan Kim: sure. i'll send the network checklist, security pack, sample terraform modules, and the pilot plan. Priya will send the benchmark workloads and we'll wait on the region list from Ravi. then schedule pilot kick-off next week.
[07:44] Ravi Patel: sounds good. Marta will confirm KMS vendor and share vendor contact. Yusuf will share CIDR and VPC peering contact.
[07:52] Jordan Kim: perfect. thanks everyone. we'll follow up by email and i'll attach the docs.
[07:58] Marta Alvarez: thanks all.
[08:00] End of call

Notes on transcript quality: occasional acronym misfires (privatelink typed "private link" or "private-ling"), speaker overlaps, some words transcribed phonetically (e.g., HSM-> "ash-em"), timestamps approximate.
notes: Customer has strict region gating (eu and apac) and won't allow cross-region fallback without explicit approval.
Security wants BYOK/HSM integration and 7-year audit log retention.
Network team prefers PrivateLink but is open to transit gateway if performance validated.
